headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said he would stop supplying chips to a customer that builds unsafe AI, though he called it a hypothetical.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record answer from the head of the dominant AI chip supplier, carried by several outlets; hedged and without a named target.
importance_line: Nvidia's chips are what AI labs depend on, so even a hedged threat to cut one off matters to those labs and their customers, but Huang named no company and set no test for what counts as unsafe.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, the dominant maker of AI chips, answered "It's a hypothetical, but yes" when asked in London whether he would halt supply to an irresponsible AI developer, adding that Nvidia would first "have a conversation" because "our technology is general-purpose." Huang also said he does not think current concern about AI safety is warranted, and Nvidia is donating US$250 million over five years in computing time to UK safety research.
